independent_elementary_implication.status: Own direct mathematical implication, not a quoted source theorem or claimed new result
independent_elementary_implication.conditions: Two joint laws P_plus/P_minus have identical observed-data marginal Q; finite second moments; m_plus(y),m_minus(y) are their posterior means. Actions range over all measurable target-vector estimators with finite squared loss. Regret subtracts each law's own Bayes/oracle squared risk.
independent_elementary_implication.proof_outline: For any delta, max exceeds the average of the two regrets. Parallelogram identity gives their average as E||delta-(m_plus+m_minus)/2||^2 + (1/4)E||m_plus-m_minus||^2. Midpoint attains the lower bound in both laws separately. Gaussianity is unnecessary.
warnings: This is oracle excess risk, not total-risk minimax; posterior variances remain in total risk.
For a selector restricted to choosing exactly m_plus or m_minus, the midpoint is inadmissible: its minimax-regret constant is generally different.
Identical single-draw observation laws stay identical under K iid repeats of the same geometry; repeated samples cannot distinguish those two laws.
For more than two priors, max-over-priors before versus after integration cannot be interchanged without justification; two-law midpoint argument alone does not establish a general minimax formula.

not_confirmed: A published theorem exactly identical to the specified Ctheta=I+theta(Q1-Q3), phase01/phase02 8-point example and every proposed constant.
A sharp general alias-block minimax task-separation theorem matching upper/lower dependence jointly on block dimension, blur, unknown PSD/calibration size and total sample budget.
Novelty of any future extension beyond these verified covered mechanisms.
